stem.en: Wind can shape solid rock in a desert. What does the cutting?

text.en: Clean moving air scrapes the rock away with nothing in it.

feedback.en: Air on its own hardly marks rock. It needs sand to cut with.

text.en: Sand grains in the wind hit the rock again and again.

feedback.en: Yes. Each grain removes very little, but thousands of years of grains wear rock away.

text.en: Hot wind melts the softer parts of the rock away.

feedback.en: Desert wind is hot, but nowhere near hot enough to melt rock.

text.en: Rain carried along in the wind dissolves the rock face.

feedback.en: Deserts get very little rain, and wind erosion works by grains hitting the rock.

explanation.en: Wind cuts rock by sandblasting. It carries sand, and the grains strike the rock thousands of times. Soft rock goes first, which leaves hard ridges called yardangs. A single stone worn the same way is a ventifact.

hints.en: Ask what the wind is carrying near the ground.
